status.label: No bug fix proposed
status.detail: The installer is correctly blocking a per-user/all-users scope conflict.

judgment.rationale: The installer log explicitly reports a per-machine PowerToys 0.65 installation and the supported cross-scope safeguard: uninstall the all-users version before installing the per-user package. This is expected installer behavior, not an update failure in PowerToys code.
evidence: The log detects DetectedPowerToysVersion 0.65.0 and a related per-user bundle 0.74.1.0.
Burn returns 0x81f40001 with the explicit message that PowerToys is already installed for all users.
judgment.recommended_action: Explain the installation-scope conflict and the supported remediation.

fix_assessment.rationale: The installer intentionally blocks mixing per-user and all-users installations; remediation is to remove the conflicting scope or use the matching machine-wide installer.

issue_context.summary: The per-user 0.101 installer refuses to run because an older all-users PowerToys installation is detected.
known_information: The log shows an existing all-users PowerToys 0.65 installation.
The attempted update uses the per-user installer.
inferences: Residual registration for older 0.74.1 may also exist, but the explicit blocking condition is the all-users installation.
issue_context.analysis: The failure message already identifies the cause. Requesting diagnostics would add no value; the maintainer action is a precise configuration explanation.
initial_investigation: Read the complete installer log in the live issue body through 2026-08-26T13:15:33Z.
No comments, assignees, linked issues, or PRs are present.
The failing condition and remediation are emitted directly by the installer.

comment.body: The log shows that `PowerToysUserSetup-0.101.2362.0-x64.exe` is a per-user installer, while PowerToys 0.65 is still registered as installed for all users. Mixing those installation scopes is intentionally blocked. Please uninstall the existing all-users installation first and then install the per-user package, or install the matching machine-wide package instead. If Apps & features no longer lists the old installation, use the documented installer cleanup/troubleshooting path for the stale registration rather than repeatedly launching the user installer.
